findings.title: Cleanup jobs now run ten times more often
findings.body: Changing the cleanup ticker from 10 minutes to 1 minute makes every cleanup job in this service run ten times as often, not just annotation cleanup. This can cause unnecessary database and filesystem load and increase contention for unrelated cleanup tasks; the interval change should be reverted or justified separately.

findings.title: Large batches exceed SQL Server's parameter limit
findings.body: For every non-SQLite database, this builds one placeholder per ID. SQL Server permits at most 2,100 parameters in a statement, so a configured cleanup batch size above that limit makes the delete fail (for example, the 32,767-sized batch used by the new test would fail on SQL Server). Handle the limit for supported dialects or chunk the IDs before executing the delete.

findings.title: Successful cleanup batches are logged as errors
findings.body: These messages use Error level even when fetching or deleting IDs succeeds, and they include every ID in the batch. Normal cleanup therefore emits error-level logs on each batch, potentially flooding error monitoring and producing very large log records for large configured batches. Log successful operations at an appropriate level and avoid logging the full ID list.
